CHIEF COMPLAINT
Acne on face

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Kayla Ward is a 18-year-old (DOB 4/28/07) presenting with acne on the face that started approximately two years ago and is present most every day. Patient reports using Persa-Gel and regular facial washing with somewhat helpful results. No associated symptoms including itching, bleeding, or pain. Acne also present on chest and back but reports it is "not too bad." Current skincare routine includes morning face wiping with water and washcloth (occasionally using elf facial cleanser if skin feels greasy) and evening routine of elf super clarity cleanser, toner, and Persa-Gel. Patient states today is a "good day" for acne. Denies acne flaring with menstrual cycle. Gets regular period for approximately two years. Mother reports the biggest acne flare occurred when patient started school sports in the fall, likely related to sweating. Mother notes patient has been compliant with facial care regimen but results have been less than desired.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
No itching, bleeding, or pain associated with acne. Remainder of examination normal.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
No additional past medical history.

MEDICATIONS
Persa-Gel, elf facial cleanser (super clarity cleanser), toner

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
No additional family history.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives with parents and sister. Pets include a dog, bird, and bunnies. In 7th grade. Participates in basketball, volleyball, and tap dancing. Wears sunscreen in summer, SPF 30.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Full exam performed except for areas under underwear and bra. Multiple benign nevi on trunk and extremities. Scattered skin-colored papules, open and closed comedones, and erythematous papules on face, primarily on forehead with some on central cheeks and chin. Chest and back relatively spared. Remainder of examination normal.

RESULTS
Mild to moderate acne, mostly comedonal with small inflammatory component. Multiple benign moles on arms, legs, back, and abdomen appearing normal with no worrisome features.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Mild to moderate comedonal acne with small inflammatory component. Plan to initiate topical therapy. Morning routine: wash face with mild cleanser, apply noncomedogenic moisturizer with SPF 30 or higher. Evening routine: wash face with mild cleanser, allow to dry, apply adapalene 0.1% cream in thin layer to affected areas, starting a few nights per week and gradually increasing to nightly use (alternative gel over the counter if cost or insurance prohibitive), follow with Persa-Gel in thin layer, then noncomedogenic moisturizer. Counseled on need for sunscreen when outside due to retinoid sensitivity and potential for dryness or irritation from adapalene. Follow-up appointment in 6 months to assess progress.
